text:
Modern laptops are getting thinner and more powerful, but this convenience comes with a hidden tax. As manufacturers solder RAM and storage directly to the motherboard to achieve sleeker aesthetics, they turn high-end machines into essentially disposable goods.

We have traded hardware autonomy for portability. Is the allure of a lightweight chassis worth losing the ability to repair or upgrade your own device? It is the ultimate tension between seamless design and user control: are we buying tools, or are we just renting hardware?
